Appendix.Content: This requires <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>p</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>x</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>></mo> <mn>0</mn> </math> wherever <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>f</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>x</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> contributes to the target integral, up to measure-zero exceptions.

If a region has nonzero integral but <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>p</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> </math> there, taking more samples from the existing support cannot repair the missing contribution. The estimator converges to the wrong target.
Stratification

Partition domain <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>D</mi> </math> into strata <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>D</mi> <mi>k</mi> </msub> </math>. A correct stratified estimator accounts for each stratum’s measure/probability. If a 3×3 pixel partition has nine equal cells but the algorithm always samples only the first five and treats their mean as the full-pixel mean, it has changed the integration domain.
Randomly selecting strata with the appropriate selection probability can remain unbiased; permanently omitting fixed strata cannot.
MIS support

Multiple importance sampling can repair a weak proposal when another technique covers the missing region and the combined estimator uses compatible PDFs. The PDFs must include discrete technique/light selection probabilities as well as continuous densities.
Debugging
Visualize sample positions and build a support occupancy histogram. Many “mysterious bias” bugs become obvious when entire regions are empty.
For image-space algorithms, also test edges/corners of the reconstruction filter, not only the pixel center.
Teach and reconstruct: Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#A missing region cannot be repaired by taking more samples there.
Related: Multiple importance sampling, Latin-hypercube sampling, Antialiasing and sample allocation.

Appendix.title: Spline bases and curve evaluation
Appendix.Content: Spline bases and curve evaluation
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: University courses · Latest development: University courses
Definition and mechanism

A spline is a piecewise polynomial curve whose neighboring pieces join under explicit continuity constraints. A cubic Bézier segment uses four control points and Bernstein weights; the weights sum to one, so the curve lies in their convex hull. A B-spline uses local basis functions so moving one control point changes only nearby spans rather than the whole curve. Knots mark where polynomial pieces meet; repeated knots reduce continuity. Catmull–Rom curves interpolate their control points and can be convenient for motion paths, while Bézier curves expose endpoint tangents through their handles. To evaluate a curve, compute basis weights at parameter <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>t</mi> </math> and take their weighted sum of control points. Position, first derivative, and parameterization speed matter separately: even a smooth path may speed up or slow down unless its parameter is adjusted.

Appendix.title: Stereo correspondence and epipolar geometry
Appendix.Content: Stereo correspondence and epipolar geometry
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: University courses · Latest development: University courses
Definition and mechanism

Stereo reconstruction uses two or more views to infer depth from corresponding image features. A 3D point and the two camera centers define an epipolar plane; its intersection with each image plane is an epipolar line. Thus a feature in one image should match along a one-dimensional line in the other, reducing a 2D search to a constrained search. With calibrated cameras, triangulation intersects the two viewing rays; noise means they are skew, so estimate the 3D point minimizing reprojection or ray distance. Depth uncertainty grows rapidly when the viewing rays are nearly parallel, which happens for distant points or small baselines. Rectification rotates images so epipolar lines become horizontal scanlines. Occlusion, repetitive texture, and calibration error can still produce mismatches, so confidence and consistency checks are essential.

This companion appears in Volume 2, The Visual Computing Bible — Volume II: Computational Geometry, Vision, Reconstruction and XR: Subdivision surface masks — Subdivision surface masks Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: University courses · Latest development: University courses Definition and mechanism Subdivision refines a control mesh and updates old and newly inserted vertices with local masks, producing a sequence that approaches a smooth limit surface. Loop subdivision targets triangle meshes: for an interior edge with endpoints <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>a</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>b</mi> </math> and opposite vertices <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>c</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>d</mi> </math>, its new point is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>3</mn> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>a</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mi>b</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>8</mn> <mo>+</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>c</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mi>d</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>8</mn> </math>. An old vertex of degree <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>n</mi> </math> becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>−</mo> <mi>n</mi> <mi>β</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mi>S</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mi>β</mi> <munder> <mo data-mjx-texclass="OP">∑</mo> <mi>i</mi> </munder> <msub> <mi>P</mi> <mi>i</mi> </msub> </math>, with the lecture’s simple weight <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>β</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>16</mn> </math> for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>n</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>3</mn> </math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>3</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>8</mn> <mi>n</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> otherwise. Catmull–Clark targets polygon meshes: face points are face-vertex averages, interior edge points average endpoints and two adjacent face points, and old vertices use face-average, edge-midpoint-average, and original-position terms. Boundary rules differ from interior masks and must be stated. Extraordinary vertices have nonregular valence and need deliberate treatment. Prerequisites

Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 2, The Foundations Bible — Volume II: Numerical Methods, Probability, Geometry and Camera Systems: Barycentric coordinates and interpolation — Barycentric coordinates and interpolation Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase6 · Latest development: University courses Definition and mechanism Barycentric weights reconstruct a triangle point as an affine combination. The weights sum to one; nonnegative weights describe points inside or on a nondegenerate triangle. Dot-system solves on off-plane inputs describe their projection, not proven surface membership. The panel sensor <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> has weights <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>5</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>12</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>4</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>3</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> and corner temperatures <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>20</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>40</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>50</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> interpolate to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>35</mn> </math>. Prerequisites
Gram matrices and coordinate metrics — Pairwise basis measurements define the systems and metric used in reconstruction. Vectors coordinates and affine points — Point, displacement and coordinate roles determine which geometric operations are meaningful.
Used by
Convex combinations and convex hulls — Builds on this mechanism in the connected geometry story. Triangle rasterization and coverage tests Ray-triangle intersection Stereo correspondence and epipolar geometry Homogeneous clipping and perspective interpolation Interpolation versus approximation ## Recall and next depth
Derive signed-area ratios; distinguish affine attribute interpolation from perspective-correct screen interpolation. Full production proofs, target-specific integration and learner mastery require further evidence. Source and navigation Teaching narrative · Coverage and source gap · Evidence and limits · Dependency Map University course development Extend the existing interpolation note with the geometric meanings that make triangle rasterization and camera calibration easier to reason about. For triangle vertices <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>p</mi> <mn>0</mn> </msub> <mo>,</mo> <msub> <mi>p</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msub> <mo>,</mo> <msub> <mi>p</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msub> </math>, a point inside can be written <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>p</mi> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>λ</mi> <mn>0</mn> </msub> <msub> <mi>p</mi> <mn>0</mn> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>λ</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msub> <msub> <mi>p</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>λ</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msub> <msub> <mi>p</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msub> </math>, where the weights sum to one and are nonnegative. Each weight is the area of the opposite subtriangle divided by the full triangle area; equivalently it is a signed edge-distance normalized by altitude. The weights therefore provide both a point-in-triangle test and attribute interpolation. They also reveal a limitation: screen-space weights do not linearly interpolate a 3D attribute after perspective projection. Interpolate reciprocal depth and attribute divided by depth, then divide the interpolated values to recover perspective-correct texture coordinates or colors. Rasterization, coverage, and depth · Textures and surface detail · Pose estimation, transforms, and robust fitting. Open Barycentric coordinates and interpolation in Volume 2

Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 2, The Visual Computing Bible — Volume II: Computational Geometry, Vision, Reconstruction and XR: Monte Carlo rendering estimators and variance — Monte Carlo rendering estimators and variance Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: University courses · Latest development: Phase 10 Definition and mechanism Monte Carlo integration estimates an integral by averaging random samples with importance weights. For target integral <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>I</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo data-mjx-texclass="OP">∫</mo> <mi>f</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>x</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mi>d</mi> <mi>x</mi> </math> and samples drawn from density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>p</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>x</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>, the estimator is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mover> <mi>I</mi> <mo stretchy="false">^</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mo>=</mo> <msup> <mi>N</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>−</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msup> <munderover> <mo data-mjx-texclass="OP">∑</mo> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mi>k</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> <mi>N</mi> </munderover> <mi>f</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msub> <mi>x</mi> <mi>k</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mi>p</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msub> <mi>x</mi> <mi>k</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>. It is unbiased when samples cover every region where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>f</mi> </math> is nonzero and the density is correct. Its variance falls approximately as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>1</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mi>N</mi> </math>, so halving standard error takes about four times as many samples. Importance sampling chooses <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>p</mi> </math> to follow the magnitude of the integrand; multiple importance sampling combines strategies such as light sampling and BSDF sampling with weights that avoid overtrusting a strategy that rarely finds a contribution. Path tracing applies these estimators to light paths, while rare caustics and narrow visibility openings remain high-variance cases. Phase 9–10 development For independent samples from density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>p</mi> </math>, the sample average estimates the integral using terms <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>f</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msub> <mi>X</mi> <mi>i</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mi>p</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msub> <mi>X</mi> <mi>i</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>p</mi> </math> is positive on the integrand support. Unbiasedness requires the support condition and integrability; finite variance additionally requires a finite second moment of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>f</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mi>p</mi> </math>. A variance estimate describes sampling spread, not systematic bias. Dependent samples add covariance terms, and multiple-importance weights combine proposal densities while preserving mixture support. A confidence interval is justified only when its sampling and moment assumptions are stated. Prerequisites

Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 2, The Visual Computing Bible — Volume II: Computational Geometry, Vision, Reconstruction and XR: Temporal reprojection and history validation — Temporal reprojection and history validation Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: XR01 · Latest development: XR01 Definition and mechanism Reprojection aligns history with a current target; disocclusion exposes content with no matching old observation. Validated blending trades noise against response/ghosting. Gaze-driven quality changes also change history reliability; TAA is not exposure integration. Prerequisites
Spatiotemporal sampling and retinal motion — Temporal reuse must respect changing scene and retinal observations. Antialiasing and sample allocation — History depends on the actual current/prior sampling strategy.
Used by
Foveated rendering and uncertainty Reservoir resampling and ReSTIR ## Recall and next depth
Derive ideal history variance and identify every violated assumption. Pending: motion/depth/jitter conventions and robust implementation. Written coverage is not a claim of learner mastery or accepted numbered-curriculum progress. Source and navigation Expanded teaching explanation · Independent coverage · Dependency Map Phase 11 camera development Reprojection predicts where a prior sample lands under camera and object motion. Depth agreement tests whether the same visible surface likely occupies that location, but cannot prove stored color remains valid after lighting, exposure, material, or sampling changes. Combine projected position, depth tolerance, and disocclusion checks; reduce history weight when confidence is low. Monocular reconstruction has arbitrary global scale, so metric depth thresholds require an external scale or consistent units. Reprojection success is geometric evidence, not a photometric guarantee. Link: A camera model must close the loop; research: Four deeper links from the TUM lecture review. Neighborhood clipping and deterministic jitter witness tools/labs/realtime_effects_reference_lab.cpp now extends history validity into two mechanisms that directly affect temporal stability. The first is deterministic subpixel jitter generated from Halton bases 2 and 3. The sample lies inside one pixel but changes frame to frame, allowing temporal accumulation to observe different subpixel locations. A jitter sequence must be owned by the camera/projection history contract: if the current and previous transforms disagree about whether jitter is included, the motion vector and reprojection become inconsistent. The second is neighborhood clipping. A reprojected history value can be geometrically valid yet photometrically stale after disocclusion or fast shading change. The smallest CPU oracle clamps the history sample into the current 3×3 neighborhood min/max interval before blending. Production TAA often uses variance-guided bounds, color-space transforms, reactive masks and velocity-dependent weighting, but the invariant remains: history should not inject values unsupported by the current local evidence. The laboratory checks known first Halton points, uniqueness over an initial sequence, bright/dark history rejection and preservation of an in-range history value. It remains a semantic oracle rather than a complete production TAA implementation.. Open Temporal reprojection and history validation in Volume 2

Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 2, The Foundations Bible — Volume II: Numerical Methods, Probability, Geometry and Camera Systems: Off-axis stereo projection and disparity — Off-axis stereo projection and disparity Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 11 · Latest development: Phase 11 Definition and mechanism Stereo cameras use two eye centres separated by a baseline, while each projection frustum is shifted so a chosen zero-parallax plane aligns in the images. Parallel eye orientations with asymmetric frusta avoid the vertical mismatch and discomfort often introduced by toe-in cameras. For rectified pinhole cameras, disparity is approximately <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi> <mi>x</mi> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>f</mi> <mi>x</mi> </msub> <mi>B</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mi>Z</mi> </math>, so inferred depth is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>Z</mi> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>f</mi> <mi>x</mi> </msub> <mi>B</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi> <mi>x</mi> </math> under the calibration and rectification assumptions. Depth uncertainty grows roughly with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>Z</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msup> </math> for fixed pixel disparity error. Distinguish interpupillary distance from lens and display-centre spacing; the rendered baseline is an optical/comfort design decision. Use consistent pixel units for focal length, baseline, and disparity before computing metric depth. Prerequisites
Stereo correspondence and epipolar geometry Camera calibration and bundle adjustment Axial depth and Euclidean range

This companion appears in Volume 1, The Foundations Bible — Volume I: From Bits to Computation, C++, Memory and Systems: Pages and page offsets — Pages and page offsets Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: C003 · Latest development: C003 Definition and mechanism A page is a virtual address block; a frame is page-sized physical backing. With page size P=2^k, divide VA into VPN=floor(VA/P) and offset=VA mod P. Translation substitutes frame identity while preserving offset. The 4-KiB examples use k=12; actual supported sizes are platform-dependent. Prerequisites

This companion appears in Volume 2, The Foundations Bible — Volume II: Numerical Methods, Probability, Geometry and Camera Systems: Multivariate Gaussian distributions and whitening — Multivariate Gaussian distributions and whitening Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10 Definition and mechanism A multivariate Gaussian is determined by a mean vector and a symmetric positive-semidefinite covariance matrix. When the covariance is positive definite, its density is an elliptical bell whose principal directions are covariance eigenvectors. Cholesky factorization maps independent standard-normal samples into correlated samples; whitening applies an inverse factor to express observations in unit-variance coordinates. Singular covariance instead confines the distribution to a lower-dimensional affine subspace and has no ordinary density with respect to full-dimensional volume. Covariance transforms as AΣAᵀ under a linear map and approximately as JΣJᵀ through a nonlinear map near a reference point. These equations support sensor fusion and projected uncertainty, but a Gaussian rendering kernel is not automatically a normalized probability density or epistemic uncertainty model. Prerequisites
Expectation, covariance, and dependence Symmetric positive-definite matrices and Cholesky Probability density and change of measure
Used by

Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 2, The Visual Computing Bible — Volume II: Computational Geometry, Vision, Reconstruction and XR: PDE fields and discrete Laplacians — PDE fields and discrete Laplacians Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: University courses · Latest development: University courses Definition and mechanism A partial differential equation constrains a field through spatial and temporal derivatives. Laplace’s equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi> <mi>u</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> </math> seeks a harmonic field whose value matches its neighborhood average; Poisson’s equation adds a source term. On a regular grid, finite differences produce the five-point stencil with four neighbor weights and a negative center weight. On a triangle mesh, cotangent weights encode angles and a mass matrix normalizes by vertex area. Boundary conditions supply essential data: Dirichlet fixes values, Neumann fixes normal flux, and Robin combines them. Neumann Laplace systems require zero net flux and a pinned value or mean because constants lie in the nullspace. Explicit heat updates have a stability-limited time step; implicit updates solve a sparse system. PDE algorithms separate field representation, spatial operator, boundary conditions, and time integration. Prerequisites
Sampling aliasing and reconstruction Convolution and filter footprints
Used by
Worlds, Images and Inference Collision barriers and continuous detection ## Full teaching explanation
PDEs, fields, and discrete solvers · Dynamics, forces, and numerical integration · Meshes, connectivity, and geometry processing Expanded direct teaching: Continuous Notes/Computing Foundations - From Bits to C++ and Systems APIs#A triangle turns a differential into a concrete field calculation. A valid finite-element cotangent stiffness can have negative edge weights while retaining nonnegative quadratic energy. Energy contraction, conservation and positivity of the evolving samples are separate requirements. The single-triangle derivation shows the distinction; the heat-step trace gives a negative sample while energy decreases.. Open PDE fields and discrete Laplacians in Volume 2

Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 2, The Foundations Bible — Volume II: Numerical Methods, Probability, Geometry and Camera Systems: Hardware depth-buffer linearization — Hardware depth-buffer linearization Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 11 · Latest development: Phase 11 Definition and mechanism Perspective projection maps axial distance nonlinearly into NDC depth. For a declared projection depth row <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>q</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mi>A</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mi>B</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mi>d</mi> </math>, solve <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>d</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>B</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>q</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mi>A</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>; finite conventional, finite reversed, infinite reversed, and OpenGL-style conventions have different coefficients or NDC conversions. The depth sample must first be interpreted in the same range and direction used by the projection matrix. This is why a single generic formula without an API and projection contract is unsafe. Verify near and far endpoints, test round trips over a range of distances, and handle an infinite-far endpoint such as reversed depth <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>q</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> </math> explicitly. Near/far endpoint checks catch sign mistakes immediately; interior round trips then test scaling and finite precision. Prerequisites
Camera view and clip-space pipeline Axial depth and Euclidean range Depth buffering and visibility order
Used by

Full teaching explanation

Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 2, The Visual Computing Bible — Volume II: Computational Geometry, Vision, Reconstruction and XR: Camera view and clip-space pipeline — Camera view and clip-space pipeline Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase7 · Latest development: University courses Definition and mechanism A camera pose maps camera coordinates to world coordinates; its inverse is the view map. Projection produces homogeneous clip coordinates, clipping applies the API-specific inequalities, and valid perspective division produces NDC. Storage order supplies none of these coordinate contracts. Reconstruction cue: A standard minus-Z perspective example needs a point in front of the camera and a meaningful clip w before division. Prerequisites
Coordinate frames and change of basis
Used by
Phase 7 teaching and laboratory Depth buffering and visibility order Lens optics and depth of field GPU vertex specification Homogeneous clipping and perspective interpolation Axial depth and Euclidean range Hardware depth-buffer linearization Screen-space ray generation and mouse picking Ray differentials and camera sampling measures
Recall and next depth Reconstruct the example, state its conventions and find an input that violates its preconditions. Deeper algorithms and measured production performance remain separate from the present model. Source and navigation Continuous explanation · Coverage and source gap · Sources and verification University course development Extend the existing transform pipeline with the clipping and depth-precision decisions that make projection robust. A view frustum is the set of points a camera can see, bounded by near and far planes as well as image sides. Transforming the frustum into a canonical clip cube makes outside tests cheap; partially intersecting triangles must be clipped and triangulated so the rasterizer still receives triangles. The near plane also avoids geometry crossing the eye plane, while the far plane limits depth range. Floating-point depth values are unevenly distributed after perspective division, so an excessively tiny near distance paired with a huge far distance can make two nearby surfaces quantize to the same depth and produce z-fighting. Choose the narrowest useful depth interval and keep the view, clip, normalized, and screen coordinates distinct. A scene description becomes an image · Cameras, projection, and calibration · Rasterization, coverage, and depth Phase 11 camera development A raster-to-ray camera maps a pixel to a geometric sample; In a pinhole model, invert projection and view transforms to recover a camera-space direction, then transform it to world space without applying translation as if it were a point. Pixel-center convention, viewport origin, handedness, clip-depth range, and normalization all affect the result. Offset a pixel to generate differential rays and estimate the surface footprint; that footprint grows with depth and changes with surface orientation. Keep ray generation distinct from raster projection while ensuring their conventions agree. Link: A camera model must close the loop; research: Four deeper links from the TUM lecture review.. Open Camera view and clip-space pipeline in Volume 2

This companion appears in Volume 2, The Foundations Bible — Volume II: Numerical Methods, Probability, Geometry and Camera Systems: Latin-hypercube sampling — Latin-hypercube sampling Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10 Definition and mechanism Latin-hypercube sampling divides each coordinate axis into <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>N</mi> </math> equal strata and uses a permutation so every sample occupies one stratum per dimension. With randomized within-stratum positions and randomized permutations, each sample has uniform marginal coordinates; samples are dependent by design. This can improve coverage for some integrands at arbitrary sample counts, including counts that do not form a square grid. It does not guarantee lower variance for every function, and IID variance formulas cannot be applied without accounting for dependence. Test exact stratum coverage deterministically, then compare estimator error over repeated randomized trials for the intended integrand. For <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>N</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>5</mn> </math>, each axis still receives five strata, avoiding the missing-cell bias of taking five cells from a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>3</mn> <mo>×</mo> <mn>3</mn> </math> grid. Prerequisites
Uniform shuffling without replacement Sampling quality: stratification, quasi-Monte Carlo, and blue noise Probability density and change of measure
Used by
Reproducible numerical benchmarking
Full teaching explanation
Design samples: without replacement, stratified, and low-discrepancy
Source coverage Supplied lesson parts: 997. Future keywords marginal stratification, randomized Latin hypercube, dependence. Open Latin-hypercube sampling in Volume 2

This companion appears in Volume 2, The Visual Computing Bible — Volume II: Computational Geometry, Vision, Reconstruction and XR: Quadric error mesh simplification — Quadric error mesh simplification Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: University courses · Latest development: University courses Definition and mechanism Quadric error simplification greedily collapses the edge with the least predicted geometric error. For each triangle plane with unit normal <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>n</mi> </math> and offset <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>d</mi> </math>, form <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>v</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msub> <mi>n</mi> <mi>x</mi> </msub> <mo>,</mo> <msub> <mi>n</mi> <mi>y</mi> </msub> <mo>,</mo> <msub> <mi>n</mi> <mi>z</mi> </msub> <mo>,</mo> <mi>d</mi> <msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mi>T</mi> </msup> </math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>K</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>v</mi> <msup> <mi>v</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msup> </math>. A homogeneous point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>U</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>x</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>y</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>z</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mi>T</mi> </msup> </math> has squared point-to-plane error <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>U</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msup> <mi>K</mi> <mi>U</mi> </math>. Sum the matrices of incident planes at each vertex; an edge candidate combines endpoint matrices. Partitioning the combined quadratic gives <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>Q</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>x</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <msup> <mi>x</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msup> <mi>A</mi> <mi>x</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mn>2</mn> <msup> <mi>b</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msup> <mi>x</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mi>c</mi> </math>, whose stationary point solves <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> <mi>x</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mi>b</mi> </math>. If the system is singular or indefinite, test endpoints and midpoint and keep the least-cost candidate. After selecting a location, reject collapses that flip incident face normals. The metric is a local approximation, so topology preconditions and orientation checks remain necessary. Prerequisites
Half-edge mesh connectivity Manifold polygon meshes and boundary structure
Used by

Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content: This companion appears in Volume 2, The Foundations Bible — Volume II: Numerical Methods, Probability, Geometry and Camera Systems: Singular value decomposition — Singular value decomposition For any real rectangular matrix, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>U</mi> <mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi> <msup> <mi>V</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mi mathvariant="sans-serif">T</mi> </mrow> </msup> </math>. Right singular vectors are input directions, left singular vectors are output directions, and nonnegative singular values are principal stretches. Unlike eigenvectors, the two sets live in different spaces. Use it when: revealing rank and conditioning, solving rank-uncertain least squares, compressing a matrix, or understanding PCA. Developed in Phase 8: The SVD expresses a rectangular map using orthonormal input and output directions joined by nonnegative stretches. Full, thin, and compact shapes have different dimensions; bidiagonal reduction and Jacobi methods compute the factors, and reconstruction, orthogonality, and triplet residuals check them independently. factor shapes · SVD algorithms and validation Prerequisites Matrix multiplication and composition order, Eigenvalues and eigenspaces, Dot products and orthogonality. Used by Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, PCA and covariance eigensystems, Polar decomposition, Matrix factorization choices. Teaching path: SVD geometry. - Matrix norms and numerical error — Extends this foundation into the Phase 8 dependency spine. - Camera calibration and bundle adjustment - Constrained optimization and inverse kinematics University course development Extend the existing factorization note with its role in estimation, conditioning, and geometry. For matrix <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> </math>, the decomposition <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>U</mi> <mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi> <msup> <mi>V</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msup> </math> separates orthogonal input directions, axis-aligned scaling, and orthogonal output directions. Singular values on the diagonal of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi> </math> quantify how strongly each independent direction is preserved; a zero or tiny value signals rank loss or poor conditioning. Least-squares fitting can use this structure to identify which parameter combinations are well constrained and to avoid amplifying measurement noise along nearly invisible directions. The same analysis explains why a camera calibration or bundle-adjustment system can have gauge freedoms: translating or scaling the entire reconstruction may leave image measurements unchanged. Singular values diagnose these ambiguities, while constraints or fixed reference poses remove them. Thus SVD links linear algebra to robust vision, not just matrix compression. Pose estimation, transforms, and robust fitting · Stereo, relative orientation, and reconstruction · Optimization, constraints, and inverse kinematics. Open Singular value decomposition in Volume 2

This companion appears in Volume 2, The Foundations Bible — Volume II: Numerical Methods, Probability, Geometry and Camera Systems: Minkowski sums and support mappings — Minkowski sums and support mappings Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: Phase6 · Latest development: Phase6 Definition and mechanism Minkowski addition combines pairwise position coordinates of sets in a common frame. Collision difference means <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mi>B</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> here. A support function returns an extreme scalar measurement; a support mapping returns a maximizing point, possibly with ties. Intervals <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">[</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>4</mn> <mo stretchy="false">]</mo> </math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">[</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>5</mn> <mo stretchy="false">]</mo> </math> have difference <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">[</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">]</mo> </math>, containing zero. Support of the difference uses a support point of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> </math> minus one of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>B</mi> </math> queried in the opposite direction. This companion appears in Volume 2, The Visual Computing Bible — Volume II: Computational Geometry, Vision, Reconstruction and XR: Light spectra and radiometry — Light spectra and radiometry Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: XR01 · Latest development: University courses Definition and mechanism Light models distinguish wave propagation, photon energy and geometrical rays. Radiometry describes physical flux/radiance/irradiance; photometry adds standardized visual weighting. RGB requires an interpretation and cannot identify a unique spectrum. Prerequisites No formal graph prerequisite. Begin with the stated units and model; this is an independent-series foundation. Used by
Reflectance and rendering equation Retinal encoding and receptive fields Optical focus and binocular conflict Color encoding and linear-light operations Probability density and change of measure Surface orientation from image brightness
Recall and next depth Explain W, W/m², W/(m²·sr), lux and nits. Pending: spectral/colorimetric calibration. Written coverage is not a claim of learner mastery or accepted numbered-curriculum progress. Source and navigation Expanded teaching explanation · Independent coverage · Dependency Map University course development Radiometry distinguishes total radiant flux <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi> </math> in watts, irradiance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>E</mi> </math> in watts per square metre, radiant intensity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>I</mi> </math> in watts per steradian, and radiance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>L</mi> </math> in watts per square metre per steradian measured with projected source area. A spectrum distributes the energy over wavelength; a three-channel RGB value is a measurement in a chosen color system and does not uniquely identify that spectrum. Solid angle measures directional extent rather than physical area. Consequently an area-light sample requires the projected-area and inverse-square Jacobian when expressed as a directional sample. Free-space radiance remains constant along an unobstructed ray, while irradiance from a point-like source changes with geometry. Photometry instead applies standardized visual weighting: luminous flux uses lumens, illuminance lux, and luminous intensity candela. These distinctions prevent treating brightness, exposure, flux and radiance as interchangeable scalar labels. Light measurement and radiometry. Open Light spectra and radiometry in Volume 2

Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 2, The Visual Computing Bible — Volume II: Computational Geometry, Vision, Reconstruction and XR: Constrained optimization and inverse kinematics — Constrained optimization and inverse kinematics Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: University courses · Latest development: Phase 9 Definition and mechanism Optimization chooses parameters to minimize an objective while satisfying constraints. Gradient descent steps opposite the gradient; Newton’s method also uses curvature, while quasi-Newton methods estimate curvature from gradient changes. Constraints may be enforced by parameterization, penalty terms, projection, or constrained solvers. In inverse kinematics, the parameters are joint angles and the objective measures distance between an end effector and its target. Forward kinematics maps angles to a hand or foot position; its Jacobian maps small joint changes to small endpoint changes. A damped least-squares step solves a stabilized linear system to reduce target error without exploding near singular poses. Joint limits, collisions, and multiple valid solutions make initialization and constraints important. The same framework applies to fitting cameras, deforming meshes, or matching image observations. Phase 9–10 development An optimization problem specifies an objective, variables, and equality or inequality constraints before an algorithm is selected. A gradient step uses first-order information; Newton and quasi-Newton steps add curvature, while line searches or trust regions control how far a local model is trusted. For nonlinear least squares, Gauss-Newton approximates curvature from the residual Jacobian and Levenberg-Marquardt damps the resulting system. Lagrange multipliers and KKT conditions describe constrained stationary points under their regularity assumptions. These local conditions do not by themselves prove global optimality. Prerequisites
Singular value decomposition Coordinate frames and change of basis
Used by

Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 2, The Visual Computing Bible — Volume II: Computational Geometry, Vision, Reconstruction and XR: Latent-variable models and generative flows — Latent-variable models and generative flows Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: University courses · Latest development: University courses Definition and mechanism Generative models describe how data could be produced, often by first sampling a latent variable <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>z</mi> </math> and mapping it to an observation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>x</mi> </math>. A variational autoencoder (VAE) learns an encoder distribution <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>q</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>z</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> </mrow> <mi>x</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> and decoder <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>p</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>x</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> </mrow> <mi>z</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>; its evidence lower bound balances reconstruction likelihood against a KL penalty that keeps the latent distribution tractable. A generative adversarial network (GAN) trains a generator against a discriminator, creating a game that can produce sharp samples but may be unstable or collapse to limited modes. Normalizing flows use invertible transformations so the data density can be computed with a change-of-variables Jacobian determinant. These methods solve different tradeoffs among likelihood, sample quality, latent structure, and optimization stability. Their assumptions matter: a VAE’s posterior family may be too simple, a GAN score is not a calibrated density, and a flow’s invertibility constrains architecture. Generated samples are not evidence that the model has learned the true causal process. Prerequisites
Probability density and change of measure Constrained optimization and inverse kinematics Research validity and ablation Automatic differentiation and backpropagation
Used by

Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 2, The Visual Computing Bible — Volume II: Computational Geometry, Vision, Reconstruction and XR: Rendering history validity — Rendering history validity A temporal renderer reuses information from earlier frames only if that information still estimates the same target quantity at the reprojected location. “Previous frame exists” is therefore not enough. History needs a validity contract. A history sample may become invalid because of:
camera cuts or projection changes; resize or dynamic-resolution changes; object transform discontinuities; newly visible or disoccluded surfaces; material or lighting changes; estimator changes such as sample pattern, exposure domain or denoiser configuration; resource reallocation or version replacement.
Reprojection is a hypothesis Motion vectors or previous transforms propose a correspondence from current sample to previous sample. The renderer should test that hypothesis with available evidence such as depth, normal, object/material identity, velocity magnitude or neighborhood statistics. A common failure is using a valid coordinate that points to the wrong surface. Bounds checking prevents memory errors, not temporal ghosting. Versioned history Treat history like a cache with a key. Relevant state changes advance a version or invalidate specific history resources. The render graph can then express that a temporal pass consumes history version N and produces version N+1. This is also important for progressive path tracing. Accumulation belongs to a camera/scene/material/light/estimator state. If any target-defining state changes and old samples remain, the output converges to a mixture of different images. Failure-oriented tests Useful temporal tests include a hard camera cut, a moving foreground object revealing background, an emissive material changing abruptly, resize, FOV change, jitter-sequence restart, and an object whose ID remains but geometry changes. For each case, record which history samples should survive and why. The existing render-graph witness proves logical resource dependencies, not temporal validity itself. Native renderer evidence should capture motion/depth/ID buffers and show the acceptance/rejection mask. Teach and reconstruct: Continuous Notes/Game Engine - From First Frame to Living Worlds#Let a renderer evolve without losing resource ownership. Related: Temporal reprojection and history validation, Reversed-Z depth contracts.. Open Rendering history validity in Volume 2

Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content: This companion appears in Volume 1, The Foundations Bible — Volume I: From Bits to Computation, C++, Memory and Systems: Build graph usage requirements — Build graph usage requirements A build target has two interfaces at once. Its source code exposes a programming interface, while its build-system target exposes the information consumers need to compile and link against that interface. In CMake terminology, PRIVATE, PUBLIC and INTERFACE describe propagation of usage requirements. They do not correspond to private/public members in C++. A PRIVATE requirement is needed to build the target itself but should not be inherited by ordinary consumers. A PUBLIC requirement is needed both by the target and by consumers because the target’s public interface depends on it. An INTERFACE requirement is consumed by downstream targets but is not used to compile the target’s own sources. Why public headers force propagation Suppose library EngineMath has a public header that includes ThirdParty/Vec.hpp. A consumer compiling only its own source plus EngineMath’s public include path still needs the third-party include directory. Marking that dependency PRIVATE may let EngineMath build while every independent consumer fails. The same reasoning applies to compile features, preprocessor definitions, generated headers and transitive link dependencies whose symbols appear in the public ABI. The test should therefore be from the consumer’s perspective: can a tiny program include the advertised public header and link using only the public target? Build graph versus include graph A textual include graph and a target dependency graph answer different questions. A source file can include a header without the build graph correctly propagating its location. Conversely, linking to a library can be required even when no source file directly includes one of its headers. Imported targets and namespaced targets are preferable to global compiler/linker flags because the dependency becomes attached to the thing that owns it. Cycles and architecture A cycle in target dependencies is often an architecture smell. Static-library cycles can also produce linker-order problems. Dependency inversion, interface targets or extracting a lower-level common module can make the ownership direction explicit. Evidence A strong build-interface test creates a minimal consumer target in a separate directory, links only the exported target, and compiles with no accidental include directories from the main project. Installation/export tests should repeat this against the installed package so the build tree cannot hide missing usage requirements. Read the connected explanation in Continuous Notes/Computing Foundations - From Bits to C++ and Systems APIs#The build graph becomes another interface. Related: C++ modules and reachability, ABI and object layout, Interface contracts and publication.. Open Build graph usage requirements in Volume 1

Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 2, The Visual Computing Bible — Volume II: Computational Geometry, Vision, Reconstruction and XR: Edge localization and subpixel contours — Edge localization and subpixel contours Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: University courses · Latest development: University courses Definition and mechanism An edge is a rapid image-intensity change, often associated with a material or depth boundary. Differentiating a noisy image amplifies high-frequency noise, so edge detectors first smooth with a Gaussian-like filter and then compute a gradient. Gradient magnitude estimates edge strength; gradient direction estimates the local normal. Nonmaximum suppression keeps a candidate only if it is a local maximum along that normal, thinning a broad response to a contour. Thresholding and hysteresis connect strong responses through weaker neighboring pixels. Subpixel localization fits a local peak to gradient samples, estimating a contour position between pixel centers. Accuracy depends on sampling, blur, contrast, and the assumed edge profile. This makes edge detection a measurement problem whose output uncertainty should propagate into later line, pose, or shape fitting. Prerequisites
Convolution and filter footprints Sampling aliasing and reconstruction

This companion appears in Volume 2, The Engine Builder's Bible — Volume II: Tools, Worlds and Living Systems: Manual Integration - Sources and Verification — Manual integration — source coverage and verification Current revision: the integrated math book has the direct textbook expansion; original bits/C++ files are retired after approval. The retained earlier corpus has 14,240 claim texts reviewed and 15,475 pending. Detailed review and integration are still incomplete. See Supplementary/Math Book Expansion - Teaching and Verification. This ledger accompanies the concept-led graphics, game-engine and combined computing-foundations volumes. It distinguishes source-body integration, direct teaching review, extracted-point comparison, and executable/numerical checks. A source being present is not a claim that every statement or repository observation is independently verified. Supplied Parts 1101–1700 All 18 supplied source bodies are retained in the expanded volumes after heading/metadata and mathematical-markup normalization. Original attachment bytes and hashes are preserved in the checkpoint. Every original fenced code body is retained unchanged. Numerical part labels are provenance, not the teaching chapter structure. The page/heading routing map and exact omitted editorial metadata remain in the checkpoint. Existing notes and proofs The pre-integration graphics and engine teaching remains in order. The combined foundations volume contains the complete substantive bodies of the original bits and C++ notes. The two original files remain available as recovery sources. Six stale references to a deleted derivations file are repaired in the combined volume by recovering the relevant saved proofs inline. Those references were not treated as evidence that the deleted file still existed. Repository-specific Kairo observations in supplied passages remain supplied snapshot claims. They were not independently recompiled or re-audited against the current Kairo repository in this integration. Code fragments are not all standalone programs. Caption and earlier book extractions The frozen input inventory contains 590 completed extraction jobs: 457 video jobs with 24,718 extracted points, and 133 book-page jobs with 4,997 extracted points. The four failed book jobs and the paused/unprocessed jobs are not silently included as complete. The extracted point text totals roughly 510,000 words. The original caption-based engine narrative is retained. The first new targeted synthesis directly checked 120 selected point IDs across 24 video sources and one Game Engine Architecture extract. One selected video source, Kohi #021, is generated ASR and is explicitly qualified. The broader comparison of all frozen extracted points is ongoing in three balanced groups; it has not yet established complete semantic coverage of the whole extraction inventory. The caption-validity audit remains a separate check: raw hashes, cue parsing and lossless cue-to-reading-span ancestry passed for its 457-source snapshot. This is not word-level audio verification. Kohi Episodes 101 and 102 remain flagged for near-duplicate association review; they are not used as distinct new teaching evidence here. Newly supplied books These seven books total 4,205 physical PDF pages. All are registered; text was mechanically made accessible where possible, and selected sections were directly read for the new teaching. None is claimed fully read or comprehensively taught in this pass. Arnold is scanned; the mechanics review actually viewed selected rendered pages. Page ranges and unread chapters are recorded in the per-topic review files. Book Physical PDF pages Current use All of Statistics.pdf 458 Selected probability, estimation, concentration, intervals and Bayesian sections Arnold Mathematical Methods Classical Mechanics 1989.pdf 536 Selected scanned rigid-body/rotation pages, physically viewed Bandit Algorithms.pdf 597 Selected confidence exploration, importance weighting, regret, nonstationarity and pure-exploration sections Book_Polygon Mesh Processing.pdf 243 Selected mesh representations, differential operators, remeshing and repair sections BV Convex Book.pdf 714 Selected convex sets, projection/separation and support-function foundations Edelcomp (1).pdf 294 Selected complexes, chains, homology, Euler characteristic and persistence sections Mathematical Methods for Physics and Engineering.pdf 1363 Selected Fourier/eigenfunction, boundary-value, heat and Green-function sections The new textbook-based narrative defines probability spaces and observation models, contrasts confidence and posterior intervals, derives importance weights, explains UCB assumptions and adaptive-stopping bias, develops mesh boundary operators and topology checks, and connects heat modes to discrete mass/stiffness operators. These additions enrich the existing subject coverage; they do not substitute for an end-to-end traversal of all seven books. Verification and concrete corrections
The original notes, supplied fenced code, normalized source-body placement, and Markdown fence balance are checked by check_preservation.py. MathJax rendering and Mermaid rendering are checked separately. Final counts are recorded in the current validation reports. Rendering success does not prove mathematical correctness. Thirty-five independent numerical witnesses check geometry, AABB transforms, normal transforms, SAH arithmetic, A* reopening, COM/inertia/impulses, damping, optional stopping, importance weighting, topology boundary maps/Betti ranks, cotangent energy and diffusion stability. The inline C++20 handle laboratory compiled with -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsanitize=address,undefined and executed its assertions without sanitizer diagnostics. Maximum 64-bit generation retirement, concurrency and GPU behavior are outside the executed test scope. Supervisor corrections include the wrong first-success sample-mean example, fixed-count versus stopped averaging, unit conversion versus physical resizing, an erroneous double-timestep number, ordinary H0 elder-rule pairing, stiffness-energy convention, ASR/caption classification, handle liveness/bounds, integer picking versus color encoding, and first-use definitions. Two new PNG/SVG teaching figures have numerical witnesses and were visually inspected. Native whole-volume Obsidian/PDF pagination and every imported C++ snippet have not been validated.

These remain explicit work rather than being hidden behind a completed extraction count. Earlier saved circle-rendering/picking and Rules of Play teaching is also integrated; the new rendering batch does not supersede older source work. Directly authored teaching follows one workshop scene through geometry, coverage, material response and light transport. New first-use explanations include samples versus fragments, barycentric versus perspective weights, projected depth, solid angle, color encoding, PDF measures, microfacet normalization, discrete light choice, reflection versus transmission support, GPU residency and scan as an allocation proof. Corrections made during this rendering pass
The supplied PBR numerical trace used mutually incompatible half-vector dot products. The replacement constructs feasible unit directions, derives the half-vector dot products, and recomputes the GGX/specular trace. Taking only the first five cells of a nine-cell stratification can bias a full-pixel estimator. Both source discussions now explain the missing support. A concrete integral has expected estimate 0.3 rather than 0.5. RGB channel roulette is described as a shared-path design choice; independently compensated channel estimators are not declared mathematically impossible. The convergence exponent distinguishes mean-square error from root-mean-square error, and reference noise/correlation/bias are qualified. The source’s placeholder matrix-tile valid mask is not a complete boundary policy. Separate left and right load masks and complete barrier participation are taught explicitly. Seven CPU matrix-oracle cases cover partial tiles and an empty inner dimension; no GPU execution is claimed. Retained direct-light loops with a positive-normal cosine are qualified as reflective-hemisphere estimators, rather than complete rough-transmission estimators. A malformed unused-field expression is repaired for MathJax. Added Markdown prose whitespace is normalized; original code bodies remain unchanged.
Primary sources checked for targeted contracts These are selected relevant sections, not a claim to have reviewed every page of each specification or textbook: Vulkan rasterization, Vulkan synchronization, Khronos shader memory layout, glTF material specification, PBRT microfacets, PBRT complete path integrator, and Nathan Reed’s depth analysis. New verification and retained earlier work validation/rendering_witnesses.py executes 20 numerical/layout witnesses, seven matrix-tile CPU emulations, nine source-body/code-preservation checks and three previous-volume preservation checks. MathJax, Mermaid and link checks are recorded separately in the validation directory. These prove the reported layer; they do not establish current Kairo/Maveb behavior, every snippet’s compilation, whole-book semantic correctness, native Obsidian performance or completed full-corpus review. The new PNG/SVG figure compares perspective interpolation, linear versus encoded averaging, and missing-strata bias; its exported image was visually inspected. Recall companions include short explanatory answers and links to the corresponding teaching and figure explanation. Earlier material is still required work. Supplementary/Manual Integration - Pending Source Queue records all 590 earlier extraction jobs and all seven mathematics books. The exact queue contains 29,715 extracted points: 14,183 claim texts read in saved reviews and 15,532 pending. All 1,180 referenced point/unit JSON files existed and were hashed when this queue was written. Claim reading, raw verification and narrative integration remain separate statuses.

Proof navigation recovery during the wider link check The wider active-file audit found stale links to the retired derivations file. Incorrect animation and platform-testing claims were rejected; historical announcements are retained as catalog/roadmap evidence, not implemented features. Animation workflow, method inputs/composition order, packaging dependencies and API capability contracts were developed in the engine/foundations books. Current claim-text totals are 14,240 reviewed and 15,475 pending, superseding the earlier snapshot counts above. This is still an unfinished whole-corpus review. Exact source/point decisions. They are added to the existing volumes: GPU-driven systems, Vulkan and Metal in Computing Foundations; render-graph architecture and editable captured-world correspondence in Game Engine; Gaussian kernels/rasterization/validation and lighting/mesh/animation in Graphics. Numeric witnesses check the projected covariance, conservative footprint radius, scan offsets, compositing order and affine covariance. Exact hashes, source partitions, complete heading registers, review artifacts and test receipts are retained under /Users/swayamsingal/.codex/source-cache/manual-integration-2026-11-10/continuation-2026-11-11/. This checkpoint extends the earlier corpus queue; it does not replace it. Supervised continuation corrections and earlier-book additions The continuation now also develops image-change certificates with explicit color/order/termination assumptions and a fixed-order compositing derivation. CPU tests execute 4,000 randomized inequality checks and explicit opacity/color/order counterexamples. Direct inspection of the reference Gaussian CUDA kernel adds a separate caveat for candidate-transmittance stopping before layer accumulation. These are mathematical and CPU bookkeeping checks, not native GPU or current project conformance tests. Earlier-book/source additions include document purpose and consistency, historical creator interviews, coupled Centipede rules, interactive writing, implicit rules and cultural values, replay/recam, player-created systems, procedural representation, camera policy and contact-response mathematics. The contact derivation distinguishes six configuration degrees of freedom from a twelve-dimensional phase state, and the kinematic constraint Jacobian from the contact-space response matrix. Its three-mass CPU witness checks the coupling terms. Other additions clarify scene save-path/write-failure policy, Euler delta rotation, framebuffer numeric types and shader program activation. Original source statements remain retained beside explicit qualifications. The live vault moved to /Users/swayamsingal/Desktop/All Might/Master during the latest resume. Current supervised checkpoint — November 12, 2026 The authoritative backlog now records 22,831 claim-text points reviewed and 6,884 pending across 590 retained records. Six additional checkpoint receipts were validated for exact claim text, source-unit membership and unchanged destination quotes/hashes. Reading, selected direct raw checks, staged deltas and published teaching remain separate; these counts are not a full-source integration certificate. The latest published additions and regression checks are recorded in Supplementary/Sources and Code Anchors#November 12 refinement — checked operations and continuous teaching. Private outstanding source reviews and full-book gaps remain in the original backlog. The referenced six Pass 10–15 texts, plus Passes 16–17, remain retained in their routed continuous volumes; retention was checked again against the original copies and normalized bodies. Reconciled claim-reading checkpoint — November 12 continuation The ledger records 26,131 claim-text points reviewed and 3,584 pending. A global check found validated earlier reading receipts that had not reached the central ledger; 1,559 distinct pending IDs were reconciled without repeating their source reads. Subsequent new checkpoints were validated separately. Source selection now uses pending IDs and excludes all staged/checkpointed IDs, replacing stale positional queues. Group 1 has no pending claim-text IDs; that does not certify exhaustive raw reading or integration of every idea. Selected teaching from shader/culling/editor sources is developed in the existing volumes; the continuation evidence records its scope. Staged spring-force discrepancies and further collision/design deltas remain awaiting supervisor review. Whole-book coverage and complete earlier-source development remain unfinished. Contact solver verification — November 12 additive continuation Two distinct C++20 contact witnesses are available in tools/labs/rigid_contact_lab.cpp and tools/labs/persistent_contact_lab.cpp, connected through the README and the source-independent narrative Supplementary/Rigid Contact - Persistent Manifolds and Solver Reconstruction. The new witness illustrates frozen impact restitution, accumulated normal and tangential impulses, two-point row coupling, feature ID carried as cache metadata, single-use warm start, and invalid-input rejection. The associated GitHub Actions workflow compiles both under strict C++20 diagnostics and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. Workflow configuration exists in the repository, but no successful GitHub-hosted run has been independently observed from this checkpoint; an empty combined status is not a pass. The solver reconstruction explicitly derives planar effective inverse mass and the Coulomb bound. A review exposed and corrected a sign error in an initial test expectation for the upward-normal / leftward-tangent example; the stored tangential scalar must be +1 for a −x impulse with tangent (−1,0). The new locally constructed witness passed six deterministic suites under a strict compiler and combined address/undefined-behavior sanitizers. The published GitHub source was then re-fetched and its key sections verified present, but an exact-byte local compilation of that connector-published file has not been established in this checkpoint; remote workflow execution is the next exact-source proof. Neither laboratory measures real-engine convergence or proves native runtime integration. The new feature identifier is not a contact matching algorithm: stale cache invalidation, 3D tangent-basis transport, fast motion/CCD, split impulses and stabilization, general scene integration, scene-set benchmark statistics, and full source-video/book reconciliation remain outstanding. The global claim-text queue and its prior reviewed/pending counts are unchanged by this targeted lab work. Supervised cache and linear CCD continuation — November 12, 2026 The additive physics verification now includes tools/labs/contact_cache_lab.cpp and tools/labs/disk_ccd_lab.cpp. The cache lab explicitly validates canonical ordered body/feature keys, previous-frame reuse, 15-degree normal-drift rejection, tangent-frame projection, bounded 0.5–2 timestep scaling, material-edit tangent invalidation, duplicate-feature rejection, stale pruning, and invalid normal rejection. Stable geometric feature IDs are assumed to be provided externally: the lab does not generate or match them. The swept-disk lab derives analytic time of impact for disks with constant relative velocity, uses a stable-root quadratic formula, and checks tunneling, frame-limited queries, misses, grazing, initial overlaps, coincident centres, Galilean invariance, large magnitudes, and invalid inputs. Its response is geometric only; it does not implement event substepping or contact impulses. Local verification: strict C++20 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror and combined AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer C++20 builds executed both new labs successfully. The published GitHub files were fetched and compared with the tested local sources using exact length and FNV-1a32 checks (the two pairs matched); file hashes are useful for byte agreement, not correctness proofs. The CCD test comment was corrected after supervision: the large-magnitude trajectory does not represent a small absolute time of impact. Both sources are registered in the repository’s contact CI workflow, but no successful remotely hosted run has yet been observed in this checkpoint. The continuous contact reconstruction chapter now explains geometric feature ownership, impulse projection into a rotated tangent, timestep policy, overlap-versus-velocity response, analytic disk CCD and finite-precision limitations in context. These added lab paths do not increment the number of reviewed source-corpus claims and do not discharge the open work on broader video ingestion, unreviewed mathematics books, full production-engine contact matching, rotating convex-shape CCD, or engine-level performance and stability. Independent source identity and second compiler check: the GitHub Git-blob SHA-1 for contact_cache_lab.cpp is 3cad6d563f3f00ef77a431dcfb48c52f0cfb926c, and for disk_ccd_lab.cpp (after correcting its comment) is 6b89db87f64897030710e646c4cc13114ad29cfa. Each matches git hash-object applied directly to the locally compiled source file, strengthening the earlier length/FNV comparison to Git’s actual full-file identity. Both sources also compiled and executed with clang++ -std=c++20 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror, independently of the default c++ run. This is two local toolchains, not a cross-platform macOS/Windows or remotely hosted GitHub Actions result. End-to-end disk event stepping and randomized supervision — November 12, 2026 An additional stand-alone C++20 laboratory at tools/labs/disk_event_pipeline_lab.cpp now connects continuous disk collision discovery to a complete fixed-duration state update. It repeatedly finds the earliest encounter among all unordered disk pairs, advances all positions to the event, groups approximately simultaneous events, freezes each incoming restitution target, runs 32 accumulated projected normal-impulse sweeps, and re-queries the remaining interval. Nine fixed scenes exercise collision timing against a static body, two-body elastic energy/momentum, symmetric simultaneous contacts, separating motion, initial overlap rejection, event budget failure, chained events, ideal inelastic response, and duplicate stable-ID / zero-duration validation. Discovered defect and correction: the first nine scenes passed, but a separately constructed deterministic 10,000-case unequal-mass isolated-pair experiment failed at trial 937. A valid impact had advanced two centres to a near-tangent configuration whose squared distance was a tiny amount below the squared combined radius; the original squared-distance tolerance rejected it as a deep overlap. The published correction computes the linear centre gap and uses a finite-precision length tolerance scaled to world-coordinate magnitude. After this correction, all 10,000 seeded cases passed under GCC and Clang and sanitizer tests. No claim is made that this tolerance is globally robust for arbitrary very large/very small coordinate ratios. The successful randomized experiment has been retained as independently executable tools/labs/disk_event_property_lab.cpp. For each isolated impact it checks exactly one event, Newton’s restitution equation, linear momentum conservation and non-increasing kinetic energy. Both newly published source files were re-fetched from GitHub and their Git blob hashes matched the locally compiled files: event pipeline e69b18ba580329db14ef0bde18811e6737790084 and property test caa2fffdfe32048e6580887ad868eda36278700f. Local strict C++20 GCC/Clang builds and combined AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer executions passed. The shared workflow is configured to run both on GitHub but its hosted execution has not yet been confirmed. The contact narrative and README now link both sources and explain the numeric trace. Remaining boundary: this is not a production Kairo world step; all-pairs event search is quadratic per rescan, contact detection is constant-velocity disk-only, friction/rotation and resting contacts are excluded, and thrown exceptions can leave the scene partially advanced. Fully robust CCD predicates, broadphase acceleration, transactional state restoration, general convex shapes, long-time stacks, numerical determinism under compiler/platform changes and runtime integration remain open. No prior video/book claim-review queue counts were incremented by this engineering experiment. Swept broad-phase candidate oracle and conservation check — November 12, 2026 The repository now contains tools/labs/swept_broadphase_lab.cpp, a tested reference implementation of constant-velocity disk swept-AABB candidate filtering. It conservatively constructs outward-rounded bounds, sorts by minimum x, tracks active x intervals and tests y overlap, then produces unique sorted candidate pairs. Each exact disk collision returned by a separately implemented analytic TOI oracle must be included in those candidates. The test covers a crossing scene, a 100-disk non-interacting scene, 200 seeded randomized 35-disk scenes, duplicate IDs and negative dt. The randomized comparison examines 200 × (35 × 34 / 2) = 119,000 possible pairs for missed collisions. GCC and Clang strict C++20 builds and a local combined AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer build passed, and the GitHub source Git-blob SHA 11f9e86dbf1ee850e64b5dafdea63427b2177187 matched the compiled local source. The CI workflow includes this new lab but no GitHub-hosted run was confirmed here. The broadphase is not integrated into the disk event stepper; it therefore establishes a conservative candidate-generation proof obligation in a small witness, not measured engine acceleration. The simple vector active set can still take O(n²) time in dense scenes, and floating-point accuracy, rapidly changing acceleration, general shapes, real scene data and production determinism remain unverified. No earlier-source corpus claims were marked reviewed solely because of this new laboratory. Three-volume implementation-depth integration — November 12, 2026 The Physics/Geometry/Mathematics lessons developed in this continuation are now directly inside the three canonical continuous notes, not only in supplementary summaries:
Mathematics: Continuous Notes/00 - From Vectors to Images - Integrated Mathematics for Visual Computing.md now contains the self-contained first-use reconstruction from a signed disk gap through stable quadratic TOI, Jacobian/effective mass, unilateral projection, swept bounds, finite-precision error policy, numerical trace and executable C++20 root laboratory. Graphics: Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography.md now includes a contact-feature/manifold clipping derivation, runnable segment clipper, numerical CCD and conservative swept-AABB proofs and the complete independent C++20 CCD and swept-broadphase code. Game Engine: Continuous Notes/Game Engine - From First Frame to Living Worlds.md now includes scene-state ownership, complete event scheduling, frozen restitution and impulses, caches and warm-starting, failure/rollback policy, a worked numerical state trace, and full embedded C++20 event stepper, persistent solver and cache implementations. This code is independent of the actual Kairo runtime.
The three large volumes were re-read after their mutations. Each new section occurs exactly once; program-code fence counts remain even (Mathematics: 366; Graphics: 1430 before the final full-code insertion; Game Engine: 4646 before the final persistent-code insertion). A syntactic fence check cannot establish Markdown/MathJax rendering or correct physics. Additions were made without deleting the pre-existing teaching bodies. The event stepper at tools/labs/disk_event_pipeline_lab.cpp now accepts useSweptBroadphase while retaining the original exhaustive mode. It builds candidate swept intervals from current body motion after each event, sorts pair IDs into the same order as the exhaustive mode and then runs the identical disk TOI and impulse functions. tools/labs/disk_event_broadphase_equivalence_lab.cpp compares four fixed scenes and 1,000 seeded scenes between modes for event count, event batches, simulated time, final centres and velocities. Strict and UBSan GitHub Actions steps are configured for that comparison. No successful GitHub-hosted run or independently compiled exact-byte post-integration binary has been confirmed in this checkpoint; code presence and test configuration are not equivalent to execution success. The previous verified local GCC/Clang/sanitizer results apply to the earlier independent labs and pre-integration source snapshots, not automatically to the newly modified event stepper. Further acceptance gates are an exact post-integration compile/run, runtime comparison against the full original deterministic suite and 10,000-case regression, actual hosted CI status, numerical stress tests for near-contact events and dense simultaneous contacts, and only then a real Kairo integration review. Global coverage constraint: these additions deepen the received collision and physics concepts and do not validate every claim in the other thousands of source pages, every downloaded lecture, or all 3,000 original parts. Previously recorded source-review gaps, mathematical-book chapters and Phase 18 parts 1701–1800 remain explicit, not declared complete. The three continuous notes are authoritative teaching routes; supplementary source ledgers and executable witnesses provide provenance and reproducibility. Three canonical volumes — additive first-use reconstruction audit (November 12, 2026) The three authoritative graphics/geometry/physics continuous volumes were edited in place rather than replaced by new per-topic notes. The Mathematics volume now adds an explicit swept-set to TOI derivation, dimensionally checked quadratic coefficients, stable-root policy, contact-space effective mass from angular impulse, projected unilateral impulses, conservative swept-bound inclusion proof, numerical wall-impact trace, and reconstruction test at the first swept-geometry encounter. Graphics now develops the broadphase/narrowphase/event-scheduler contracts, body identity and buffer ownership, no-false-negative property tests, time-of-impact/debug trace, finite-precision tolerance failure, and CPU/GPU evidence requirements beside its existing swept-geometry section. Pre-existing Markdown code fences and display-math boundary counts were unchanged; Game Engine gained exactly four correctly formed code-fence boundaries.
